en: Now, this is it for this Deno core API
module. We had a look at some of the core
APIs built into Deno and you hopefully got
an understanding of how Deno works and what
Deno is
when we use it in code.
It gives us a couple of low-level APIs which
we can use to work with user input, to set
timers, to write to a file,
send a network request if we wanted to, to
convert data, that's all baked into Deno.
And as you can imagine, with these features,
you can basically build everything because
if you think about bigger apps,
in the end, they all come down to
listening some input, sending some requests,
creating some files.
This is in the end what all programs do.
But as I also mentioned throughout this
module, we don't wanna write all that
low-level code on our own all the time. And
that is very cumbersome and error-prone.
We rather wanna focus on our core business
logic. And therefore in the next module,
we'll take a big step towards that goal by
diving into the standard library.
And there we will then also start working on
our first web server.
